<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|108|THE GOSPEL|CHA. VIII.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=8|verse=14}}† And they forgot to take bread: and they had but one loafe vvith them in the boate. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=15}}† And he commaunded them, saying, Looke vvel and bevvare of the leauen of the Pharisees, and the leauen of Herod. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=16}}† And they reasoned among them selues saying, Because vve haue not bread. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=17}}† Which {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving, saith to them, Why doe you reason, because you haue not bread? do you not yet knovv nor vnderstand? yet haue ye your hart blinded? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=18}}† hauing eies see you not? and hauing eares heare you not? Neither do you remember? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=19}}† When {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 6, 38.''}}* I brake fiue loaues among fiue thousand: and hovv many baskets ful of fragmēts tooke you vp? They say to him, Tvvelue. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=20}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 8, 5.''}}* When also seuen loaues among foure thousand, hovv many maundes of fragments tooke you vp? And they say to him, Seuen. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=21}}† And he said to them, Hovv do you not yet vnderstand?

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=22}}† And they come to Bethsaida: and they bring to him one blinde, and desired him that he vvould {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Our Sauiour vsed to worke much by touching: that we may learne not to cōtemne the corporal and external application of holy things, nor to chalēge by the spirit and faith only, as Heretikes doe.}}∷ touche him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=23}}† And taking the hand of the blinde, he led him forth out of the tovvne: and spitting into his eies, imposing his hands, he asked him if he savv any thing. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=24}}† And looking vp, he said, I see men as it vvere trees, vvalking. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=25}}† After that againe he imposed his hands vpon his eies, and be began to see, and vvas restored, so that he savv al things clerely. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=26}}† And he sent him into his house, saying, Goe into thy house: and if thou enter in to the tovvne, tel no body.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=27}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 16, 13. Lu. 9, 18.''}}* {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent forth and his Disciples into the tovvnes of Caesarêa-Philippi: and in the vvay he asked his Disciples, saying to them, Whom do men say that I am? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=28}}† Who ansvvered him, saying, Iohn the Baptist, some Elias, & other some as it vvere one of the Prophets. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=29}}† Then he saith to them, But vvhom do you say that I am? Peter ansvvering said to him, Thou art Christ. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=30}}† And he threatened them that they should not tel any man of him.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=31}}† And he began to teache them, that the Sonne of man must suffer many things, and be reiected of the Auncients and of the high Priestes and the Scribes, and be killed: and after three daies rise againe. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=32}}† And he spake the vvord openly. And Peter taking him, began to rebuke him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=33}}† Who turning, and seeing his Disciples, threatened Peter, saying, Goe behind me Satan, because thou sauourest not the things that are of God, but that are of men. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=34}}† And calling the multitude<noinclude>{{rh|||together}}</noinclude>
